outcome: The general Hilbert-Smith conjecture remains open; the only relevant 2024 work found (Shelukhin's 'A symplectic Hilbert-Smith conjecture') proves cases in a restricted symplectic-topology setting (Hamiltonian homeomorphisms on symplectically aspherical manifolds / standard symplectic tori), which is a related problem in a changed setting rather than a restriction of the stated topological-manifold conjecture.
summary: The Hilbert-Smith conjecture (as stated: any locally compact group acting continuously and faithfully on a topological manifold is a Lie group) remains open in general as of September 2026. The known partial results — Montgomery-Zippin/Bing for dimensions 1-2, Repovš-Ščepin (1997) for Lipschitz actions, Martin (1999) for quasiconformal actions, and Pardon (2013) for the 3-manifold case — all predate the 26 January 2024 frozen revision and are not new events in this window. The one arXiv item the triage flagged, Egor Shelukhin's 'A symplectic Hilbert-Smith conjecture' (arXiv:2403.07195, v1 submitted 2024-03-11, v2 2024-06-26, with an appendix by Leonid Polterovich), proves that the p-adic integers Z_p admit no non-trivial continuous action by Hamiltonian homeomorphisms on symplectically aspherical symplectic manifolds, and more generally that a locally compact group acting faithfully by homeomorphisms in the C0-closure of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms on certain symplectic manifolds (e.g. standard tori) must be a Lie group. This changes the hypotheses of the original statement in two ways at once: the acting maps are restricted to a specific C0-closure of Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms (not arbitrary homeomorphisms), and the target is restricted to symplectically aspherical manifolds with symplectic-topology structure (Floer cohomology, barcodes, Hofer's metric) rather than arbitrary topological manifolds. Per SS3.1 this is a related problem obtained by changing the question, not a case obtained by restricting it — it does not remove territory from the general conjecture's domain (arbitrary continuous actions on arbitrary manifolds), so it does not count as a change to this problem. I searched further for any 2024-2026 developments (proof announcements, disproofs, counterexamples, AI involvement) and found none: Terence Tao's blog has only a single 2011 post tagged with this conjecture and nothing later; a 2026 Simons Foundation survey of Hilbert's problems does not cover the Hilbert-Smith conjecture (a separate, later-named conjecture) at all; general searches for AI/machine-learning involvement in this conjecture returned nothing relevant. No AI system appears anywhere in the material connected to this problem in the window.
competing_reading: One could argue the Shelukhin result is a 'case' of the Hilbert-Smith conjecture in the loose sense that Hamiltonian homeomorphisms are a subset of all homeomorphisms, so ruling out actions by p-adic integers via this subset is technically ruling out a subset of the possible actions covered by the general conjecture, which could be read as narrowing the space of potential counterexamples to the full statement. However, the paper's own framing and methods are specific to symplectic topology (symplectic asphericity, Floer cohomology, Hofer's metric) and do not bear on faithful actions by homeomorphisms in general on general manifolds, which is the substance of the stated conjecture and is precisely why the field itself treats this as a distinct 'symplectic Hilbert-Smith conjecture' rather than as partial progress on the classical one.
what_would_settle_it: A paper that proves the conjecture (or a genuine dimensional/class-of-groups case of it) for actions by general homeomorphisms on general topological manifolds, extending beyond dimension 3 or beyond the already-settled Lipschitz/quasiconformal cases, would resolve the ambiguity; absent that, the symplectic result is best read as adjacent rather than as progress on the stated bullet.
